attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own essay, concluding his reasoning about Anthropic's fundraising and prepayments.

semantics.note: The wording roughly follows the sentence, but dropping 'really' makes it read like a literal claim about which entity is listing. In context it is an evaluative point that the S-1 picture is unrepresentative. That is rhetoric, not a testable observation.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no unique support or contradiction test. It names no measure, degree of difference or comparison date, and it does not narrow the claim against the speaker.

evidence.note: The S-1 describes a shift to direct accelerator procurement. That makes the concern intelligible, but it cannot settle an evaluative comparison.

reviews.rationale: This is an evaluative, rhetorical characterisation with no defined measure, threshold or comparison date. Changing operations described in the filing cannot show that the company is or is not 'really' the one described. It cannot be scored, but the case itself is not broken.

attribution.note: Zitron's own calculation and attribution in his essay. He quotes the S-1 separately as his source.

semantics.note: Keeps 'as much as' as an upper bound, the ~$33.08B base, the 7% figure, and the specific attribution to distillation. Reading 'to date' as Jan–Sep 2026 fits the heading and the quoted disclosure.

contract.note: The plain reading (nine-month realised revenue, upper bound of the estimate) is ordinary and fair. Requiring that the distillation share itself be established is fair, because the speaker named that specific category.

evidence.note: The S-1 gives $16.286B first-half revenue and 5–7% for nine months, but for all policy-violating customers. That category is broader than distillation.
Press report, sourced to the FT, of $16.8B Q3 revenue. Supports the revenue input only, not the distillation share.
Reproduced FT report: Anthropic told investors distillation was 5–7% of revenue. The period is not identified, so it does not contradict the claim but does not settle it.

reviews.rationale: The arithmetic holds: $16.286B + $16.8B ≈ $33.09B, and 7% ≈ $2.32B. But the filing's 5–7% covers all policy-violating customers. The FT's distillation-specific 5–7% has no stated period. Neither source alone ties a ~7% share of Jan–Sep revenue to distillation, as the contract requires. The figures line up suggestively, but nothing contradicts the claim and nothing settles it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own estimate in his essay, derived from the reported value of the lease deal.

semantics.note: 'At least $5B next year' is firm. The $10B and $30B figures are qualified and kept as such. Payments go through a financed lease vehicle rather than straight to Broadcom; the contract accounts for this. The unclear-timing qualifier is kept.

contract.note: Calendar 2027 for 'next year' and a firm $5B minimum is an ordinary reading. Treating $10B and $30B as qualified, untimed possibilities is fair to the speaker.

evidence.note: Broadcom/bank announcement dated 2026-10-26: deliveries are expected from 2027. It gives no 2027 payment amounts and is a company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: The forecast concerns 2027 payments, and 2027 had not begun by the 2026-10-28 evaluation date. No verified payments or irreversible event meets the early-resolution rule. The announced 2027 delivery timing is only context. The forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. He cites Anthropic's S-1 language as backing but endorses the conclusion himself.

semantics.note: 'Guaranteed' is unhedged, so the financial part is a firm forecast with an open horizon. The 'bait-and-switch' clause is an evaluative allegation that is bundled in and is not testable in the same way.

contract.note: Using Q2 2026 as the baseline follows the surrounding passage. The contract fairly flags that the metric definitions are unspecified and that there is no deadline, so interpretation shapes the result.

evidence.note: Reuters report of Q3 revenue and adjusted profitability. It concerns a quarter that ended before the claim, so it cannot show the forward trajectory.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline ('going forward'). No financial results after the claim were available by the evaluation date, and Q3 data predates the claim. No conclusive event closes the trajectory. The deception allegation has no evidence of intent either way.
